stories.title: 📜 以斯帖记（希腊文增补） 1
summaryBullets: 末底改是一位流亡中的犹太人，他梦见一场大冲突，两条巨龙准备争斗，但一道溪流涨成洪水，带来了拯救（1:1–11）。
crossRefs: 创世记 41:1–32 — 梦作为神圣的预兆。
但以理书 2:28 — 神揭示奥秘。
以斯帖记 6:1–3 — 末底改的忠诚后来被想起。

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: תַּנִּין (tannîn, 'dragon/serpent') — Greek: δράκοντες (drákontes) — Aramaic: תניניא (tannīnyā)
translationNotes.note: 末底改异象中代表对立势力的象征性形象，后来被解释为哈曼和末底改。

stories.keyTakeaway: 末底改的梦预示着以色列即将面临的危险和拯救，他对国王的忠诚也由此确立。

stories.title: 📜 以斯帖记（希腊文增补） 2
summaryBullets: 后来，末底改发现两名太监密谋反对亚达薛西王；他将此事报告国王，阴谋者被处决（2:1–23）。
国王将此事记录在年代志中，末底改的忠诚得以被记载。
crossRefs: 创世记 41:1–32 — 梦作为神圣的预兆。

stories.title: 📜 以斯帖记（希腊文增补） 3
summaryBullets: 哈曼崛起掌权，密谋灭绝犹太人（3:1–15）。
crossRefs: 以斯拉记 9:6–15 — 为民族之罪的认罪。
但以理书 9:4–19 — 流亡中的代祷。
希伯来书 4:16 — 坦然无惧地来到神的宝座前。

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שַׂק וָאֵפֶר (śaq wāʾefer) — Greek: σάκκος καὶ σποδός (sákkos kai spodós) — Aramaic: שק ואפר (saq wʾapr)
translationNotes.note: 在整部希伯来经文中使用的传统哀悼和忏悔标志。

stories.keyTakeaway: 末底改和以斯帖恳切祈求神的帮助，因为灭绝的谕令威胁着以色列的存亡。

stories.title: 📜 以斯帖记（希腊文增补） 4
summaryBullets: 末底改身穿麻衣，撒上灰烬，为这一谕令哀恸（4:1–11）。
末底改祈祷，承认以色列的罪过，恳求神施行拯救（4:12–20）。
以斯帖也祈祷，承认自己的软弱，祈求神赐她在王面前的勇气（4:21–30）。
她决心代表自己的民族去见王，即便冒着生命危险（4:31–17）。
crossRefs: 以斯拉记 9:6–15 — 为民族之罪的认罪。
但以理书 9:4–19 — 流亡中的代祷。
希伯来书 4:16 — 坦然无惧地来到神的宝座前。

stories.title: 📜 以斯帖记（希腊文增补） 5
summaryBullets: 第三天，以斯帖穿上王后的礼服进入朝廷；她因恐惧而晕倒，但神使她蒙恩（5:1–2）。
王向她伸出金杖，和蔼地接见了她（5:3–4）。
以斯帖邀请王和哈曼赴宴，为提出请愿做准备（5:5–8）。
哈曼因自己的荣宠而骄傲，进一步密谋对付末底改，搭建了绞架（5:9–14）。
crossRefs: 创世记 32:11 — 雅各恐惧却祈求拯救。
尼希米记 2:1–5 — 酒政在王面前的恐惧。
箴言 21:1 — 王的心在神手中。

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שַׁרְבִיט זָהָב (šarbîṭ zahāb) — Greek: σκῆπτρον χρυσοῦν (skēptron chrysoûn) — Aramaic: שרביטא דדהבא (šarbīṭā d’dahabā)
translationNotes.note: 王权的象征；以斯帖的生死取决于王是否做出接纳的手势。

stories.keyTakeaway: 以斯帖在王面前冒着生命危险，但神使她蒙恩，而哈曼的阴谋仍在继续。

stories.title: 📜 以斯帖记（希腊文增补） 6
summaryBullets: That night the Lord took sleep from the king, so he told his teacher to bring the book of daily records and to read to him. (6:1).
He found the words written about Mordecai, how he had told the king about the two royal eunuchs who were on guard and sought to lay hands on Artaxerxes. (6:2).
The king said, “What honor or favor did we bestow on Mordecai?” The king’s servants said, “You have not done anything for him.” (6:3).

While the king was inquiring about the goodwill shown by Mordecai—Look! Haman was in the courtyard. The king asked, “Who is in the courtyard?” Now Haman had come to speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on the pole that he had prepared. (6:4).
The servants of the king said, “Look! Haman is standing in the courtyard.” And the king said, “Summon him.” (6:5).
Then the king said to Haman, “What shall I do for the person whom I wish to honor?” And Haman said to himself, “Whom would the king wish to honor more than me?” (6:6).
So he said to the king, “For a person whom the king wishes to honor, (6:7).
let the king’s servants bring out the fine linen robe that the king wears and the horse on which the king rides, (6:8).

and let them be given to one of the king’s honored Friends, and let him robe the person whom the king loves and mount him on the horse, and let him proclaim through the open square of the city, saying, ‘Thus shall it be done to everyone whom the king honors.’ ” (6:9).
Then the king said to Haman, “You have spoken well! Do just as you have said for Mordecai the Jew who serves at court. And let not a word of what you have said be omitted.” (6:10).

So Haman got the robe and the horse; he put the robe on Mordecai, mounted him on the horse, and went through the open square of the city, proclaiming, “Thus shall it be done to everyone whom the king wishes to honor.” (6:11).
Then Mordecai returned to the courtyard, but Haman returned home, mourning and with his head covered. (6:12).

Haman told his wife Zosara and his friends what had befallen him. His friends and his wife said to him, “If Mordecai is of the Jewish people and you have begun to be humiliated before him, you will surely fall. You will not be able to defend yourself, because a living god is with him.” (6:13).
While they were still talking, the eunuchs arrived and hurriedly brought Haman to the drinking party that Esther had prepared. (6:14).

stories.title: 📜 以斯帖记（希腊文增补） 7
summaryBullets: So the king and Haman went in to drink with the queen. (7:1).

And the second day, as they were drinking wine, the king said, “What is it, Queen Esther? What is your petition, and what is your request? It shall be granted to you, even to half of my kingdom.” (7:2).
She answered and said, “If I have found favor with the king, let my life be granted me at my petition and my people at my request. (7:3).

For we have been sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, plundered, and made slaves—we and our children—male and female slaves. I took no heed, but now our adversary brings shame on the king’s court.” (7:4).
Then the king said, “Who is the person who would dare to do this thing?” (7:5).
Esther said, “Our enemy is this evil man Haman!” At this, Haman was terrified in the presence of the king and queen. (7:6).
The king rose from the banquet and went into the garden, and Haman began to beg for his life from the queen, for he saw that he was in serious trouble. (7:7).

When the king returned from the garden, Haman had thrown himself on the couch, pleading with the queen. The king said, “Will you dare even assault my wife in my own house?” Haman, when he heard, turned away his face. (7:8).

Then Bugathan, one of the eunuchs, said to the king, “Look, Haman has even prepared a pole for Mordecai, who gave information of concern to the king; it is standing at Haman’s house, a pole fifty cubits high.” So the king said, “Let Haman be executed on that.” (7:9).
So Haman was hung on the pole that had been prepared for Mordecai. With that the anger of the king abated. (7:10).

stories.title: 📜 以斯帖记（希腊文增补） 8
summaryBullets: 哈曼倒台后，王将哈曼的产业赐给以斯帖，并提拔末底改（8:1–2）。
以斯帖为她的民族请命；王颁布反谕令，授权犹太人自卫（8:3–12）。
谕令的副本被分送到各省，犹太人因此欢欣荣耀（8:13–17）。
crossRefs: 出埃及记 17:9–14 — 以色列抵御亚玛力人。
以赛亚书 54:17 — 凡为攻击你造成的器械必不利用。
罗马书 8:31 — 神若帮助我们，谁能敌挡我们呢？

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: גְּזֵרָה (gəzērāh, 'decree') — Greek: διάταγμα (diátagma) — Aramaic: גזרתא (gəzerātā)
translationNotes.note: 正式的王室谕令，以书面形式发出并加盖印章，在波斯律法中被视为不可撤销。

stories.keyTakeaway: 末底改的反谕令推翻了哈曼的阴谋，为犹太人带来了安慰和尊荣。

stories.title: 📜 以斯帖记（希腊文增补） 9
summaryBullets: Now on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is Adar, the letter written by the king arrived. (9:1).
On that same day the enemies of the Jews perished; no one resisted, because they feared them. (9:2).
The governors of the satrapies, the princes, and the royal secretaries were paying honor to the Jews, because fear of Mordecai weighed upon them. (9:3).
The king’s decree required that Mordecai’s name be held in honor throughout the kingdom. (9:4).
Now in the city of Susa the Jews killed five hundred men, (9:6).
including Pharsannestain, Delphon, Phasga, (9:7).
Pharadatha, Barea, Sarbacha, (9:8).
Marmasima, Aruphaeus, Arsaeus, Zabutheus, (9:9).
the ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha, the Bougean, the enemy of the Jews—and they indulged themselves in plunder. (9:10).
That same day, the number of those killed in Susa was reported to the king. (9:11).

The king said to Esther, “In the city of Susa, the Jews have destroyed five hundred people. What do you suppose they have done in the surrounding countryside? Whatever more you ask will be done for you.” (9:12).
And Esther said to the king, “Let the Jews be allowed to do the same tomorrow. Also, hang up the bodies of Haman’s ten sons.” (9:13).
So he permitted this to be done and handed over to the Jews of the city the bodies of Haman’s sons to hang up. (9:14).
The Jews who were in Susa gathered on the fourteenth and killed three hundred men but took no plunder. (9:15).

Now the other Jews in the kingdom gathered to defend themselves and got relief from their enemies. They destroyed fifteen thousand of them on the thirteenth of Adar but did not engage in plunder. (9:16).
On the fourteenth day of the same month they rested and kept it as a day of rest with joy and gladness. (9:17).
The Jews who were in the city of Susa came together also on the fourteenth but did not rest. They celebrated the fifteenth with joy and gladness. (9:18).

On this account, then, the Jews who are scattered around the countryside keep the fourteenth of Adar as a joyful holiday and send presents of food to one another, while those who live in the large cities keep the fifteenth day of Adar as their joyful holiday, also sending presents to one another. (9:19).
Mordecai recorded these things in a book and sent it to the Jews in the kingdom of Artaxerxes both near and far, (9:20).
to institute these days as holidays and to keep the fourteenth and fifteenth days of Adar, (9:21).

for on these days the Jews got relief from their enemies. The whole month (namely, Adar) in which their condition had been changed from sorrow into gladness and from a time of distress to a holiday was to be celebrated as a time for feasting and gladness and for sending presents of food to their friends and to the poor. (9:22).
So the Jews accepted what Mordecai had written to them: (9:23).
how Haman son of Hammedatha, the Macedonian, fought against them, how he made a decree and cast lots to destroy them, (9:24).
and how he went in to the king, telling him to hang Mordecai, but the wicked plot he had devised against the Jews came back upon himself, and he and his sons were hanged. (9:25).

Therefore these days were called “Purim,” because of the lots (for in their language this is the word that means “lots”). And so, because of what was written in this letter and because of what they had experienced in this affair and what had befallen them, Mordecai established this festival, (9:26).

and the Jews took upon themselves, upon their descendants, and upon all who would join them to observe it without fail. These days of Purim should be a memorial and kept from generation to generation, in every city, family, and country. (9:27).
These days of Purim shall be observed for all time, and the commemoration of them shall never cease among their descendants. (9:28).
Then Queen Esther daughter of Aminadab along with Mordecai the Jew wrote down what they had done and gave full authority to the letter about Purim. (9:29).
And Mordecai and Queen Esther established this decision on their own responsibility, pledging their own well-being to the plan. (9:31).
Esther established it by a decree forever, and it was written for a memorial. (9:32).

stories.title: 📜 以斯帖记（希腊文增补） 10
summaryBullets: 末底改被高举，地位仅次于王，并致力于同胞的福祉（10:1–3）。
开篇的梦得到解释：两条巨龙代表末底改和哈曼；那道溪流代表神的拯救（10:4–13）。
crossRefs: 创世记 41:32 — 梦由神所印证。
以斯帖记 6:6–11 — 末底改受到王的尊崇。
诗篇 126:1–3 — 神欢喜地恢复锡安。

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: תַּנִּין (tannîn, 'dragon/serpent') — Greek: δράκοντες (drákontes) — Aramaic: תניניא (tannīnyā)
translationNotes.note: 被解释为末底改和哈曼的象征，代表着最终由神的拯救所化解的冲突。

stories.keyTakeaway: 叙事以末底改被高举和他的梦应验作为结尾，显明了神对以色列的拯救。
